acceptance: This computer's device connection dials out with only the device key (a device-signed challenge, then a signed hello), serves tunnels and refuses the old plaintext file and execution frames, and stops on request. A device this computer holds no key for never connects. A clock that is off borrows the Cloud's once; a bad signature, a clock that stays off, an unexplained 403 or an outage are retried with the same identity and never taken for a revocation; only a revocation close or a device_revoked refusal stops for good, and close 4005 stops it as outdated. Each admitted tunnel is handed to the SSH server as a byte stream; tunnels for a folder not shared or past the limit are refused; a malformed frame, a silent Cloud or an unexpected close end the connection, which comes back with a fresh challenge. A gateway outside the PuppyOne host family is never dialled.

reason: TS's connector follows system sleep: it drops the socket on suspend and reconnects at once on wake. The native connector is not wired to the system's power notifications; after a sleep the dead socket is found by the 30 s silence (or a failed heartbeat write) and the connection comes back through the ordinary retry.

acceptance: Another computer runs only what this one allows, over its SSH session: a command or a terminal (a shell or a known Agent launcher, with a pty) needs the folder's write and shell or Agent capability and runs in the folder, with its output, errors and exit status coming back; a launcher that is not one is refused, a missing Agent is reported as launcher_unavailable rather than starting something else, and with no execution service (no sandbox) nothing starts while the session lives on. Unsharing the folder ends what it allowed. Every spawn is wrapped in the folder sandbox, with no unsandboxed tier, and shell history kept out of the owner's own. The terminal client starts a shell or an Agent by launcher, relays input as bytes, resizes, and reports how it ended. The sandboxed Git adapter cannot run Git when merely constructed and has no unsandboxed fallback.

The folder-tier sandbox never falls back to running unsandboxed (no sandbox: sandbox_unavailable). Seatbelt's profile allows writing only the folder, temporaries, caches and the Agent's own state, and puts the protected credential paths and the App's data after every allowance so they always win. Bubblewrap binds everything read-only but the folder, caches and Agent state, hides credentials (a folder under an empty tmpfs, a file under /dev/null), starts in the folder and runs the program after "--". Each Agent's own state is known; a shell has none. A real shell in this computer's sandbox writes only the folder and cannot read a credential.
